extracted.intended_audience: business leaders, managers, workers, and general readers interested in industry, labour relations, and education (early 20th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive principles and evaluative criteria for education, democracy, industry, labour organization, and management practices as argued in a popular business memoir. Provides standards for judging leaders, strikes, unions, and the aims of education and production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Able man defined by ability to do things
rubrics_metrics.description: "An able man is a man who can do things, and his ability to do things is dependent on what he has in him. What he has in him depends on what he started with and what he has done to increase and discipline it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability is both innate and cultivated; practical competence and disciplined development matter more than titles or credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education's purpose: teach thinking not facts
rubrics_metrics.description: "The object of education is not to fill a man's mind with facts; it is to teach him how to use his mind in thinking."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: College should act as an "intellectual gymnasium" to develop mental muscle; true education continues after school through the discipline of life; mental activity and the ability to apply knowledge are valued over accumulation of facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid two extremes about education
rubrics_metrics.description: "There are two extremes to be avoided: one is the attitude of contempt toward education, the other is the tragic snobbery of assuming that marching through an educational system is a sure cure for ignorance and mediocrity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect education's role in developing capacity but avoid blind reverence for credentials or disdain for experiential learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge ≠ mental activity
rubrics_metrics.description: "Great piles of knowledge in the head are not the same as mental activity. A man may be very learned and very useless. And then again, a man may be unlearned and very useful."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuate the productive use of knowledge; beware of 'overloading' with facts that hinder practical thinking and action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational test: usefulness to humanity
rubrics_metrics.description: "What can you do to help and heal the world? That is the educational test."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure education by a person's ability to hold up his own end and to help others; mastery of a sphere of work equates to having 'won his degree'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge is available to any willing learner
rubrics_metrics.description: "If a man is born with normal human faculties... there is no knowledge within the possession of the race that he cannot have--if he wants it!"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-directed learning and willingness to use the tools of letters (reading/writing) make knowledge accessible; lack of learning is often lack of will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propaganda that lacks facts is self-destructive
rubrics_metrics.description: "Propaganda that does not spread facts is self-destructive. And it should be."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public argument and organizational persuasion must be grounded in facts; competing sets of ideas should be pooled to construct sound opinions rather than one-sided propaganda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy = equal chance by ability; emphasize service
rubrics_metrics.description: "I am for the kind of democracy that gives to each an equal chance according to his ability. I think if we give more attention to serving our fellows we shall have less concern with the empty forms of government..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Democracy judged by opportunity and service rather than slogans; practical service reduces focus on class distinctions and political forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class labels are largely fictional; judge by work and character
rubrics_metrics.description: "The 'rich' and the 'poor' are both very small minorities... We have men who will work and men who will not. Most of the 'classes' that one reads about are purely fictional."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid simplistic class-based propaganda; evaluate people by their habits of work and contribution rather than wealth labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critique of professionalized union leadership
rubrics_metrics.description: "The only strong group of union men in the country is the group that draws salaries from the unions... Some of them are very rich. ... Others ... border on Bolshevism and anarchism--their union salaries liberating them from the necessity of work so that they can devote their energies to subversive propaganda."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between rank-and-file working members and salaried union officials; be suspicious of officials whose interests diverge from the membership.

rubrics_metrics.name: True labour leader leads to work and wages, not strikes
rubrics_metrics.description: "The only true labour leader is the one who leads labour to work and to wages, and not the leader who leads labour to strikes, sabotage, and starvation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership should promote productive employment and fair rewards; the ideal union is one of interdependent interests tied to usefulness and efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justifiable strike: remedy for proper conditions and just rewards (usually employer's fault)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The strike for proper conditions and just rewards is justifiable... These justifiable strikes are usually the employer's fault."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strikes that draw attention to genuine injustices can be morally justified but ideally should not be necessary if employers do their job; such strikes indicate managerial failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strike manipulated by speculators (hidden design)
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is a second kind of strike--the strike with a concealed design... The motive may be the personal greed of the speculators or they may want to change the policy of a business because its example is embarrassing to other employers..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for strikes that cannot be settled and that serve third-party speculators aiming to weaken or take control of an industry; outside suppliers being tied up can be a sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strike provoked by money interests to discredit labour
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is a third kind of strike--the strike that is provoked by the money interests for the purpose of giving labour a bad name."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to efforts by financial interests to incite extreme labor actions to alter public sentiment against workers; consider motives behind escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 'Soldiering' and idleness do not create jobs; industriousness creates opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is sometimes said that the less a worker does, the more jobs he creates for other men. This fallacy assumes that idleness is creative. Idleness never created a job. It creates only burdens."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage efficiency and industriousness; reorganizing for efficiency creates growth and new employment; loafing and artificial restriction of output harms the public and job creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: A day's work = equivalent service for the wage
rubrics_metrics.description: "A day's work means more than merely being 'on duty'... It means giving an equivalent in service for the wage drawn."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both overwork and shirking upset labor-management equivalence; maintaining honest equivalence is essential to business stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management shares blame with labour for loss of equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: "Management must share the blame with labour. Management has been lazy, too... It found it easier to hire an additional five hundred men than to so improve its methods..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employers must improve methods and efficiency rather than inflate labor costs; public bears cost of mismanagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strikes that pass burden to the community are ultimately unsuccessful
rubrics_metrics.description: "A strike which brings higher wages or shorter hours and passes on the burden to the community is really unsuccessful. It only makes the industry less able to serve--and decreases the number of jobs that it can support."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When strike gains are funded by the public or reduce industry capacity, the long-term effect is negative for employment and service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business as a 'holy trust' providing livelihoods
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is something sacred about a big business which provides a living for hundreds and thousands of families... the continuance of that business becomes a holy trust."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large productive organizations should be treated as responsibilities beyond individuals; continuity, honest management, and protection of employees' livelihoods are paramount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer justified only while able to steer the business properly
rubrics_metrics.description: "The employer is but a man like his employees... He is justified in holding his job only as he can fill it. If he can steer the business straight... then he is filling his place."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge management by competence in running the enterprise and securing workers' security; unfit employers cause more harm than unfit employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony must not stifle competition and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: "You can hardly have too much harmony in business. But you can go too far in picking men because they harmonize... The organization is secondary to the object."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations should prioritize the common objective and allow constructive thrust and counterthrust (competition); excessive emphasis on pleasant atmosphere can sap energy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical acts count more than 'glad hand' propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: "We do not believe in the 'glad hand,' or the professionalized 'personal touch'... Propaganda, bulletins, lectures--they are nothing. It is the right act sincerely done that counts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tangible benevolent actions that cost management something and benefit all prove good intentions; avoid superficial sentimentalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference policy toward unions with fair wages and hours
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have no antagonism to unions, but we participate in no arrangements with either employee or employer organizations... The wages paid are always higher than any reasonable union could think of demanding and the hours of work are always shorter."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain direct relations with employees rather than formal arrangements with union officials; respect unions' aims but avoid external interference in plant relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to war until actual declaration; duty to support after entry
rubrics_metrics.description: "I believe that it is the duty of the man who opposes war to oppose going to war up until the time of its actual declaration... When our country entered the war, it became the duty of every citizen to do his utmost toward seeing through to the end that which we had undertaken."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition to war can be principled until national involvement is formalized, after which citizens owe duty to national efforts; fighting does not in itself resolve underlying questions.
